enhanced.fullText:
The Export Administration Act of 1979, codified at 50 U.S.C. § 4601 et seq., establishes the primary statutory framework for controlling exports of dual-use items and technologies that could serve both civilian and military purposes. While the original Act expired, its provisions continue under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (50 U.S.C. § 1701) and have been modernized by the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 (50 U.S.C. § 4801 et seq.).

The Act empowers the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) within the Department of Commerce to administer the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) at 15 CFR Parts 730-774. These regulations control exports of items listed on the Commerce Control List (15 CFR Part 774) and apply to all U.S. persons, including higher education institutions, regardless of location.

For universities, compliance is critical given extensive international research collaborations, foreign student populations, and technology transfer activities. The regulations cover physical exports, deemed exports (release of controlled technology to foreign nationals within the U.S.), and re-exports of U.S.-origin items. Key provisions include licensing requirements for controlled items (15 CFR Part 748), export control classification requests (15 CFR § 748.3), and recordkeeping obligations (15 CFR Part 762).

Higher education institutions must establish export control compliance programs addressing research security, visiting scholars, international partnerships, and technology licensing. The fundamental research exclusion (15 CFR § 734.8) provides limited relief for basic research ordinarily published, but applied research and restricted access projects typically require licenses.

Violations carry severe penalties under 50 U.S.C. § 4819, including criminal fines up to $1 million per violation, imprisonment up to 20 years, and civil penalties up to $300,000 or twice the transaction value. Administrative sanctions may include denial of export privileges, effectively barring institutions from international activities.

Recent amendments under the Export Control Reform Act strengthen controls on emerging technologies, expand extraterritorial jurisdiction, and enhance enforcement capabilities. Universities must monitor the Entity List (15 CFR Part 744, Supplement 4) restricting transactions with designated foreign parties and comply with new foreign direct product rules affecting research collaborations.
enhanced.summary: Federal law controlling exports of dual-use technologies through licensing requirements. Universities must comply when conducting international research, hosting foreign nationals, or transferring controlled technologies.
enhanced.requirements:
## Export Control Classification
- Determine Export Control Classification Numbers (ECCNs) for research technologies and equipment
- Submit classification requests to BIS when uncertain (15 CFR § 748.3)
- Maintain current classifications for all controlled items

## License Requirements
- Obtain export licenses for controlled technology transfers to restricted destinations
- Apply for deemed export licenses when sharing controlled technology with foreign nationals
- Ensure license compliance for re-exports of U.S.-origin items

## Screening and Due Diligence
- Screen research collaborators, visiting scholars, and international partners against Entity List
- Conduct end-use/end-user verification for technology transfers
- Document screening procedures and maintain records

## Institutional Compliance Program
- Designate export control officers responsible for oversight
- Establish policies covering research, partnerships, and international activities
- Provide training for faculty, researchers, and relevant staff
- Implement pre-award review procedures for sponsored research
enhanced.reportingRequirements: No routine periodic reporting required. Event-triggered obligations include: license applications submitted via SNAP-R system when exporting controlled items; voluntary self-disclosure of violations within reasonable time of discovery per 15 CFR § 764.5; annual compliance certifications if subject to settlement agreements.
